newsitem.title: FRANCE: French shares end lower on U.S. NAPM upset.
newsitem.headline: French shares end lower on U.S. NAPM upset.

text.p: French shares ended in loss on Friday, pushed down by falls in the bond markets, following a stronger-than-expected U.S. NAPM reports which indicated upward price pressures, traders said.
The National Association of Purchasing Management's index soared to 58.6 in July versus 55.7, suggesting there was a lot of strength in the U.S. economy. The news suggested inflationary pressures.
The market had been steady before the report, clawing back losses sustained after the publication of U.S. July non-farm payrolls which showed higher jobs growth than the market expected.
The CAC-40 index closed down 26.33, or 0.85 percent, at 3,049.44. The index was up 0.78 percent on the week.
The CAC-40 August futures contract down 28 at 3,054 from Thursday's close.
Total volume was a fairly high 10 billion francs.
Pay-television company Canal Plus shed 3.09 percent to 1,161 francs. Some brokers pointed to the disappointing growth in new subscribers and revenue shown in the first-half sales figures.

Alcatel Alsthom put in a sparkling performance, adding 6.18 percent to 859, wooing the market with a 17 percent rise in first-half sales. A number of brokers, including DB Bourse, Cheuvreux de Virieu and Ferri, set share price targets around 1,000 and upgraded the stock.

Retailers fell to profit-taking, with Carrefour falling 1.6 percent to 4,118, Promodes down 2.33 percent to 2,430, Pinault-Printemps Redoute down 1.78 percent, and Casino shedding 1.54 percent. British broker Robert Fleming downgraded Carrefour to a sell from a buy last month, when the stock was trading at 4,400.
Bic closed up 4.11 percent at 532, helped by the planned acquisition of U.S. penmaker Sheaffer, which will increase its dollar exposure.

Renault benefited from July car sales figures which showed its sales advanced in the domestic market and exports to other European markets rose 13 percent, or double the six percent growth in the overall market. The carmaker firmed 0.35 percent to 173.
PSA Peugeot Citroen fell 2.51 percent to 698.
